Chapter 3: Managing Attention—Creating Space for Deep Focus
Now that we've talked about picking your daily Highlight, there’s a new obstacle: actually giving it the attention it deserves. In a world packed with distractions and constant pings, just finding focus can feel like a superpower, right? So, how do you carve out space for what matters most?
Think of your attention like a spotlight. If you shine it on just one thing, that thing becomes sharp and clear. But if you try to light up everything, it all turns into a dull blur. What you want is a way to let that spotlight shine right on your Highlight, without being pulled in a thousand directions.
One of the best ways to do this is by creating what I call “Focus Blocks.” These are chunks of time—maybe just an hour, maybe a bit more—set aside just for your Highlight. And here’s the secret: they don’t have to be marathon sessions. Even 60 to 90 minutes of true, undisturbed focus can lead to some of your best work. The real trick is protecting that time like it’s the most important meeting on your calendar.
How can you build and defend your own Focus Blocks? Here are a few simple tactics that make a big difference:
First, actually schedule your focus time. Block it out on your calendar, and treat it as if it’s an unmovable appointment—because it is.
Next, set clear boundaries. Let the people around you—whether that’s coworkers, family, or roommates—know when you’re in focus mode, and kindly ask not to be interrupted.
Then, prepare your space. Clear off anything you don’t need, turn off those pesky notifications, and close any tabs or apps that might tempt you away.
And finally, start with a simple ritual. Maybe you make a cup of tea, or just take a few deep breaths. Whatever it is, let it be your signal that you’re shifting into deep work mode.
Of course, it’s not just the outside world that distracts us. Sometimes, our own minds pull us away—worries about other tasks, the itch to check messages, or just the urge to multitask. Becoming aware of these habits is half the battle. When you notice them, you can gently guide your attention back to what’s most important.
Here’s a practical tip: keep a notepad nearby. Whenever a distracting thought pops up—like remembering an errand or feeling the urge to check your email—just jot it down and promise yourself you’ll come back to it later. It’s a surprisingly powerful way to keep your mind clear.
Another mindset shift is what I like to call “Laser Mode.” Imagine your focus time as something truly special—a high-priority mission. Give yourself permission to be fully present, and let go of the need to respond to every message the second it arrives. Not everything needs your attention right away.
And don’t forget: everyone’s natural rhythms are different. Some people do their best thinking early in the morning, while others hit their stride in the afternoon or evening. Try experimenting with different times to see when deep focus feels easiest for you. Once you know your sweet spot, schedule your Focus Blocks to match.
Over time, these little habits add up. They make it easier and easier to slip into deep focus and protect the attention you need to make real progress on your Highlight.
Up next, we’ll dive into the other side of the equation: how to cut down on those sneaky distractions that threaten to throw you off track, no matter how well you’ve planned.
